rationale: bugs_open/230, re-verified live today: the fleet's 61 discovery checks across three site-discovery agents have NO recurring driver — 0 of 5 scheduled rows targeting them are enabled (all hand-made oneshots), no CronJob runs them, and every discovery orchestration in the 24h retention window is hand-fired at exactly the sites lanes were already working. A broken page on an unattended site is never re-detected: finetuning.uk (a deployed customer site) serves two pages with 334-byte empty sections today, findEmptySections' own predicate returns both, and no work item exists. The designed driver (improvement-sweep) is 'intentionally paused during core build' (register IMP-016) and cannot simply be flipped back on: it is the whole detect-triage-fix loop whose drain decision is recorded as PENDING with the owner in bugs_open/083, its site selection starves (IMP-010: ORDER BY sites.updated_at, and nothing it does advances its own sort key), and its <50-open-items cap permanently excludes the busiest sites — measured today: webdesign.co.uk 85, dartsonline.com 79 open build items, i.e. the two most-worked sites would never be examined. This change gives DETECTION a clock and touches nothing else: a fair-rotation stamp table + three scheduled_tasks rows (one per discovery agent, hourly tick, one least-recently-selected site per tick, 7-day per-site period, observe-only — findings land exactly where each check already puts them, dedup-guarded), plus a daily watchdog CronJob that makes the two silent failure shapes visible (a site falling out of rotation; selections that stop producing runs). Zero Go changes — the scheduler's pre_query/data-modifying-CTE mechanics are used exactly as built and as already exercised by database-cleanup and stuck-task-reaper. Measured cost: one full discovery cycle = 2 LLM calls (~4.2k in / ~2.1k out tokens); steady state ~9 site-examinations/day fleet-wide. NOTE ON SCOPE/FORCE: this submission carries no platform/ files BY DESIGN (config + one CronJob); FORCE=1 was used because the client-side path filter is a credit guard, and a change that starts firing agents fleet-wide on a clock deserves the guardian's eyes regardless of which directory it lives in.

plan.summary: Site discovery has no recurring driver (bugs_open/230), so sites stop being examined when humans stop looking. Add migration 346: a site_discovery_rotation stamp table plus three enabled scheduled_tasks rows giving the three discovery agents a fair hourly rotation over active/deployed sites (7-day per-site period, stamp-on-selection so a failing site cannot starve the fleet, busy-skip that defers rather than excludes, observe-only detection). Add a daily site-discovery-staleness-check CronJob (modelled on single-owner-carriers-check) that reports any site out of rotation and any window where selections advance but no discovery orchestrations appear. The improvement-sweep row and the bugs_open/083 promotion/drain question are deliberately untouched.

edits.rationale: The rotation needs durable per-(site,agent) state: COMPLETED orchestrations purge at 24h (database-cleanup step 3) so orchestration history cannot key a 7-day rotation, and sites.updated_at is IMP-010's starvation defect. Stamp-on-SELECTION (not completion) so a site whose run fails cannot pin the rotation head — the bugs_open/048 shape the scheduler's own comments warn about. Three tasks, one per agent, so each agent's coverage is independent; enabled=true because seeding disabled rows recreates the oneshot graveyard this bug documents, and every knob is a one-UPDATE pause listed in the runbook.
edits.sketch: CREATE TABLE site_discovery_rotation (site_id uuid REFERENCES sites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, agent_type text, last_selected_at timestamptz NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (site_id, agent_type)); INSERT 3 scheduled_tasks rows named site-discovery-rotation-{quality,design,completeness}: target_topic=system.agent.scheduled.requests (the proven oneshot envelope), interval 3600, concurrency_group site-discovery max_concurrent 1, enabled, fire_message. pre_query per agent: WITH due AS (SELECT s.id, s.domain FROM sites s LEFT JOIN site_discovery_rotation r ON r.site_id=s.id AND r.agent_type='<agent>' WHERE s.status IN ('active','deployed') AND COALESCE(r.last_selected_at,'-infinity') < now()-interval '7 days' AND NOT EXISTS (claimed build item) ORDER BY r.last_selected_at ASC NULLS FIRST, s.id LIMIT 1), stamped AS (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) SELECT sid::text AS site_id, domain FROM due. Guard: DO/RAISE asserts table present, exactly 3 enabled rows, each pre_query references its own agent_type and the stamp table; BEGIN/COMMIT wraps all. Dry-run proven against live data today: first pick robot-hands.com, stamp advances, second pick differs, 2 busy sites deferred; all three STORED pre_queries EXECUTEd successfully, then rolled back.

edits.sketch: DELETE FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name LIKE 'site-discovery-rotation-%'; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS site_discovery_rotation; guard asserts both gone.

edits.rationale: The stamps are written by the pre_query BEFORE the Kafka fire, so they are fire-and-forget (the recorded landmine: last_triggered_at keeps advancing while nothing runs). A watchdog outside the mechanism must ask the two questions the stamps cannot answer. A discovery check cannot do this job — a check that reports discovery-not-running can never run when discovery is not running.
edits.sketch: Daily: (1) coverage — any active/deployed site with stamp missing/older than 2x period for any agent -> finding; grace of one period after task creation so the install day does not fire 60 false positives; (2) closers-vs-producers — stamps advanced in last 24h with zero discovery orchestrations in the same 24h retention window -> finding; (3) driver_missing — fewer than 3 enabled rotation tasks or table absent -> finding (this is 230's original state and the check proved it live today, exit 1, before the migration was applied). One doc_notes row per run on findings AND clean (a missing row means the job did not run); exit non-zero on findings. Same image/secret/reporting conventions as single-owner-carriers-check.

plan.risks: 1) This turns on fleet-wide examination-on-a-clock (enabled=true at seed). Blast radius is bounded and measured: max one site per agent per hourly tick, ~2 LLM calls per full cycle, concurrency_group max_concurrent 1; pause is one UPDATE. A reviewer who thinks enabled=false-pending-owner is safer should weigh it against this bug's own mechanism: the estate's five previous discovery rows are all disabled one-offs nobody re-enabled. 2) Observe-only means the detected pile grows with true findings for item types whose promoter is parked (bugs_open/083) — stated in the bug files rather than hidden; the alternative (wiring promotion) would pre-empt a pending owner decision and add a fourth triage_detected_items carrier, which RFC_006 ruled against. 3) Discovery checks were last mass-run in an attended context; a check that misbehaves on some site now fires unattended — mitigated by dedup on insert (idx_swi_dedup), by detection writing rows rather than mutating sites, and by the one-UPDATE pause. 4) The busy-skip reads site_work_items.status='claimed' AND pipeline='build'; if a claim leaks (never released), its site defers until the claim reapers clear it — claimed-item-timeout (120s) and stale-work-item-reaper (3600s) exist, and the watchdog's 2x-period threshold catches the residual case. 5) The stamp is selection, not completion: a silently dropped fire (chassis restart ~300s window) delays that site one period; recurring drops are what the closers-vs-producers check exists to catch, within a day.
